title: Multiple LEFT JOINs
flavorText: Be careful when chaining LEFT JOINs. Once you go LEFT, stay LEFT to avoid accidentally filtering rows.
narrative: List all customers, their orders (if any), and the quantity of 'Widget's in those orders (if any).
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, tier TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, quantity INTEGER);
seedSql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','Gold'),(2,'Bob','Silver'),(3,'Charlie','Bronze'),(4,'Diana','Gold'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (101,1,'Shipped',150.0),(102,2,'Pending',80.0),(103,1,'Delivered',200.0),(104,NULL,'Cancelled',50.0); INSERT INTO products VALUES (10,'Widget',25.0),(20,'Gizmo',50.0),(30,'Doodad',10.0); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (101,10,2),(101,20,2),(102,10,1),(102,30,5),(103,20,4);
task: Select customer name, order id, and quantity. LEFT JOIN from customers to orders, then LEFT JOIN to order_items (but ONLY for product_id = 10, which is 'Widget'). Order by customer name, order id.

hints.text: customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON ... LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id AND oi.product_id = 10
Make sure product_id=10 is in the ON clause of the second LEFT JOIN, not the WHERE clause.
SELECT c.name, o.id, oi.quantity FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id AND oi.product_id = 10 ORDER BY c.name, o.id;
